answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by authenticating peers through directional millimeter-wave links between high-elevation nodes on a mesa and an oasis receiver. Verifiers evaluate spatial angle-of-arrival and phase delays on synchronized radio pulses, forcing an adversary to deploy discrete, physically steered antenna hardware per identity. However, thermal turbulence and refractive ducting at dawn distort wave trajectories, occasionally triggering false verification failures.
